obtained.how: university repository: Dalhousie University's DalSpace (Scholaris) open PDF of the thesis scan (148 pages, OCR text layer with heavy noise); Appendix 1 values read on the page image

bibliography.checked_against: the thesis title page (PDF p. 3) and Dalhousie's release form (PDF p. 4)
bibliography.note: John Morgan Cooley, Ph.D. thesis, Department of Biology, Dalhousie University, Fall 1973 (release form dated 4 September 1973). Title as in the entry ('Leptodiaptomus minutus Lillj. (Copepoda: Calanoida) in Bluff Lake, Nova Scotia').

claims.claim: L. minutus breeds 'intensely late in winter under ice or early in spring'
claims.quote: breeding intensely late in winter under ice or early in spring
claims.conditions: Cooley's summary of the species' life cycle across its range (Newfoundland, Experimental Lakes Area, Clear Lake, Bluff Lake), describing 'an overwintering population, primarily adult'
claims.note: the same sentence goes on: breeding continues until late fall; summer egg production is 'quite low' but may rise again in the fall

claims.claim: in unstratified Bluff Lake, Nova Scotia
claims.source_value: mostly unstratified: about 75 % of the 4.8-ha lake lies above 4 m and stays unstratified all year; the deepest point (7 m) stratifies in summer (Fig. 2 isotherms; Table 6 refers to the lake 'when stratified')
claims.location: p. 11 (PDF p. 24), Fig. 2 caption; p. 76 (PDF p. 101)
claims.quote: Approximately 75% of Bluff L. is above 4m and remains unstratified
claims.conditions: small oligotrophic seepage lake near Halifax (no inlet, a trickling outlet), sampled October 1970 to May 1972
claims.note: write 'mostly unstratified' or 'shallow (75 % above 4 m), largely unstratified'

claims.claim: adults overwintered, subitaneous eggs appeared from February and hatched in March, the first generation matured from mid-August
claims.location: p. vi (PDF p. 11), Abstract; p. 23 (PDF p. 37)
claims.quote: began producing subitaneous eggs in February which hatched in March
claims.conditions: Bluff Lake, 1970–72; the next words: 'to provide a first generation of animals that developed slowly; and began maturing in mid-August'

claims.claim: from mid-October every egg was a diapausing egg
claims.quote: continuous from Feb. until mid-October when all eggs produced become
claims.conditions: recruitment from subitaneous eggs February to mid-October; p. 42: 'By Oct. 11 all eggs collected from live plankton samples were in diapause' (1971); egg production stopped in mid-November

claims.claim: in Bluff Lake the calanoid's diapausing eggs hatched in March after a 4 °C chill
claims.source_value: in the lake they hatched in March (late February in the Discussion, p. 80), with the subitaneous eggs; the chill is a laboratory result: eggs moved to 14 °C never hatched without prior time at 4 °C, but eggs kept at 8 °C (no 4 °C) began hatching after 6 months, and none hatched in under about 1 month whatever the treatment
claims.location: p. 51 (PDF p. 69); p. 50 (PDF p. 68), Table 13; p. vi (PDF p. 11), Abstract
claims.quote: incubated at 14 °C ever hatched unless they had a prior cold treatment
claims.conditions: laboratory, diapausing L. minutus eggs collected 28 Oct–4 Nov 1971, held dark or lit at 4, 8 or 14 °C; under-ice lake temperatures were not recorded (equipment failure, Fig. 2)
claims.note: suggested: 'hatched in March; in the laboratory they needed a cold period (4 °C, or 6 months at 8 °C) before warmth'

claims.claim: in Bluff Lake the overwintering adults, not the eggs, carried the population
claims.quote: production of diapausing eggs does not appear to be absolutely necessary
claims.conditions: estimated diapausing eggs deposited in fall 1970 and 1971: at most 380 and 450 (×10²/m²), against 4,384 and 2,280 (×10²/m²) subitaneous eggs laid by the overwintering adults; sediment traps suggested about half the diapausing-egg estimate

claims.claim: adult Leptodiaptomus minutus lost ~0.0005/day Nov–May in Bluff Lake (and overwinter on lipid)
claims.location: p. 89 (PDF p. 115); Appendix 1 (PDF p. 138), 'Cor Ad' column
claims.quote: calculated by assuming that their maximum numbers were 580
claims.conditions: Appendix 1's corrected adult totals, a smooth curve drawn by eye through scattered counts: 580 ×10²/m² on 15 Nov 1970 (and through 20 Feb 1971), 560 in March, 540 from mid-April, 530 on 15 May; the overwintering adults had no recruitment until August
claims.note: ln(580/530) / 181 d (15 Nov → 15 May) = 0.00050 d⁻¹. The raw adult counts scatter widely (e.g. 885, 981, 793, 545 in Feb–Mar), so the rate is that of the hand-smoothed curve. 'On lipid' is not from Cooley, who does not discuss lipid; Grosbois et al. 2017 (also cited) must carry it

notes: Other values: Bluff Lake 4.8 ha, max 7 m, Secchi 0.3–4.3 m, pH 5.3–6.8 (Tables 1–2). L. minutus 'multivoltine': three 1971 cohorts; mortality greatest May–October, partly from Epischura nordenskioldi and Mesocyclops edax. Development time and dry weights of each instar are in Tables 8–9 and 17–19. The thesis text is an OCR'd typescript: quote digits from the page images.
